answer: At each dawn a public beacon fires one unpredictable pulse, and every identity is permanently assigned its own disjoint millisecond window in which it alone must sign that pulse live from its own compute. One operator piloting many clones cannot hit N separate precise windows at once from shared hardware: the scheduler jitters, clones miss their slots, and their padded stake drains away like water through karst. Honest independent agents each hold a single window and keep full weight.
